sense: a show, the performing of a play or music

evidence: Cic. Mur. 72: spectācula sunt tribūtim data
terms.comment: Any show put on for an audience, in the theatre or the circus; spectāculum committere, to begin the show (Livy). A concert is concentus (see concert).

terms.grammar: phrase: agō with fābulam; passive, fābula agitur, the play is on
evidence: Ter. Hec. 33: cum prīmum eam agere coepī
Plaut. Men. 72: dum haec agitur fābula (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A play is data when it is first put on (Ter. Hec. 1–2) and agitur while it is being performed.

phrases.latin: haec cum data nova est, novum intervēnit vitium et calamitās, ut neque spectārī neque cognōscī potuerit
phrases.english: when this play was first put on, a new mishap and disaster intervened, so that it could neither be watched nor followed

phrases.latin: ut pompā, lūdīs atque ejus modī spectāculīs teneantur ob eamque rem vel famem et sitim perferant
phrases.english: (we see children) held by a procession, games and shows of that kind, and putting up even with hunger and thirst for their sake

sources: Lewis & Short: spectaculum · Lewis & Short: ago
